name: No post-incident review or review actions not tracked to closure
description: Incidents were closed without a recorded root-cause review, or a review was held but the actions arising were recorded only in the review document and cannot be shown to have closed.

may_assert: That incidents meeting the entity's own review threshold have no recorded review, where the incident population has been supplied.
That review actions have no owner, target date, or closure evidence.
That actions from a prior review remain open beyond their target date with no risk acceptance.
must_not_assert: That the incident will recur. The observation concerns whether the cause was addressed, not the likelihood of repetition.
That a formal post-incident review is required by SOC 2 for every incident. The entity's own threshold governs.

escalates_to.when: No review process exists at all, so no incident would ever produce a root-cause assessment.

de_escalates_to.when: Reviews are said to have occurred but the records have not been supplied.

severity_factors.criterion_impact: CC7.5 concerns recovering from incidents and developing remediation; restoring service without addressing cause leaves the second half unmet.
severity_factors.pervasiveness: One low-severity incident without review differs from no review process operating at all.
severity_factors.detectability: Detectable by reconciling the incident population against review records and action closure.
escalates_when: A high-severity incident has no review
Actions repeat across successive reviews, indicating the cycle never closes
de_escalates_when: The incident fell below the entity's own review threshold
Actions were tracked in the normal engineering backlog and closed
Root cause was addressed through an existing tracked workstream

detection_signals.signal: Incidents at or above the review threshold with no linked review record.
Review actions recorded with no owner, target date, or closure evidence.
Root cause identified but no corresponding change to configuration baseline or detection rules.
Respondent describes reviews held informally with actions kept in the review document.

auditor_impact: Auditors commonly trace an incident through to its review and then to the closure of the resulting actions. Actions held only in a document rather than a tracked backlog are a frequent point of challenge.
customer_impact: The condition that allowed an incident affecting the customer's data remains, so the same failure can recur.
false_positive_guidance: Not a gap where the incident fell below the entity's own documented review threshold; the threshold is the entity's to set.
Not a gap where actions were tracked in the normal engineering backlog rather than in an incident-specific list; reconcile across systems before concluding.
Not a gap where the root cause was already being addressed by an existing workstream and the review references it.
A period with no declared incidents produces no population here. Report that the control had no operating population, not that it failed.

source_refs.supports: Typical auditor treatment, severity factors, and detection approach.

notes: DriftGuard finding archetype. DriftGuard produces observations against it; only a service auditor issues findings.
